context: 5 Future Work and Open Questions In [8], the main complexity measure was actually the running time and not the success probability. Our results about equilibria are also relevant to this measure, but the social gain is different. For example, it is still true that A? is an equilibrium under the exclusive policy, and that all other symmetric equilibria in the exclusive policy are equivalent to it. As A? is optimal among symmetric profiles w.r.t. the running time, the PoSA of Cex is equal to the PoSS, and it is also the best among all policies. Furthermore, importing from [8], we know that the PoSA (w.r.t. the running time) is about 4. However, showing the analogue of Corollary 7, namely, that the PoA of Cex is that achieved by A? , seems difficult, especially because general equilibria are not necessarily greedy. Moreover, the results of Vetta [31] do not apply when analyzing the running time, and finding the PoA, PoSA, and PoSS of the sharing policy, for example, remains open. Another interesting variant would be to consider feedback during the search. For example, assuming that a player visiting a box x knows whether or not other players were there before. Such a feedback can help in the case that the players collaborate [5], but seems to significantly complicate the analysis in the game theoretic variant. Finally, we would like to encourage game theoretical studies of other frameworks of collaborative search, e.g., [4, 6, 7, 15].
